base_estimator_decision: Base estimator: sklearn.linear_model.LogisticRegression(max_iter=2000, random_state=<config.train_seed>), default L2 penalty, C=1.0 (sklearn's own default). No pre-specified base-classifier/architecture for Two-Step PU or PU-Bagging was found in docs/PU_AOP_RESEARCH_CONTEXT.md, the Planner doc, or the proposal (inspected directly before writing this module, not assumed). Logistic regression was chosen over a tree ensemble (e.g. RandomForestClassifier) because it is the more common choice in the original Two-Step PU (Elkan & Noto 2008) and PU-Bagging (Mordelet & Vert 2014) literature, is simpler to reason about and faster to fit/reproduce exactly, and keeps both new baselines on the SAME base-estimator family for a cleaner later comparison between them. Wrapping the existing torch BinaryMlp as a scikit-learn estimator merely to force architectural uniformity with PN/nnPU was explicitly considered and rejected as a disproportionate engineering detour for a baseline-implementation task -- see docs/IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md's Task 4.4 decision log entry.
label_encoding_note: y=1 encodes an E1/E2 labeled positive; y=0 encodes a C1 row passed to the scikit-learn/pulearn estimator's unlabeled-surrogate slot. This 0 is a library-API numeric requirement (pulearn's PU estimators accept exactly one 'unlabeled' numeric code and have no three-way positive/unlabeled/negative label type), not a project-level claim that C1 is a confirmed negative -- see AGENTS.md rule #1 and this module's own docstring.

seed_context.note: Determinism is controlled entirely via BaggingPuClassifier(random_state=..., n_jobs=1) and LogisticRegression(random_state=...); no separate global numpy/torch seed call is needed or made by this module.

training.no_learning_curve_reason: PU-Bagging's .fit() is a single, non-iterative procedure that internally trains n_estimators bootstrap members in one call -- there is no per-epoch optimization trajectory to plot, unlike PN/nnPU's mini-batch training loops. The ensemble's own internal validation signal (out-of-bag score) is reported in oob_metrics instead of a held-out loss curve.

limitations.assumed_unlabeled_c1: C1 is an assumed-negative/PU-unlabeled pool, NEVER experimentally confirmed antioxidant-inactive. Both algorithms' first internal stage trains a classifier treating C1 rows AS IF negative -- a standard, documented step of Two-Step PU/PU-Bagging themselves (Elkan & Noto 2008; Mordelet & Vert 2014), not a project-level reclassification of C1's status.
limitations.evidence_tiers: E1 (assay-confirmed) and E2 (provisional benchmark-annotated) positives are POOLED as labeled positives, identical policy to nnPU (Task 4.3), but their provenance/counts remain separately auditable (class_counts.e1_train/e2_train/...). E2 is not uniformly assay-confirmed.
limitations.base_estimator_not_binarymlp: Two-Step PU and PU-Bagging wrap sklearn.linear_model.LogisticRegression, NOT models.BinaryMlp -- a documented, deliberate departure from PN/nnPU's shared architecture (see each baseline module's own BASE_ESTIMATOR_DECISION_NOTE and the Task 4.4 decision log). Comparing these baselines' scores to PN/nnPU numerically must account for this architecture difference, not just the label-assumption difference.
limitations.no_mcc_auprc_here: This task (4.4) implements and sanity-checks the baselines only. MCC/AUPRC computation and a cross-baseline comparison table are Task 4.5's explicit scope, not performed here.
limitations.shortcut_bias_risk: FR2 (Task 2.5) documented substantial FR1-positive-vs-C1 distributional differences (length, charge, GRAVY, aromaticity, composition); neither algorithm automatically eliminates those differences.
limitations.evaluation_scope: Fold-0-only initial baseline. Full C1/C2/C3 cross-pool comparison, calibration, RNIS, and five-fold validation are out of Task 4.4's scope.
limitations.scientific_sign_off: Technical acceptance only -- no supervisor or scientific sign-off is implied for the chosen base estimator, hyperparameters, or any scientific conclusion.
